item.title: Cunningham-less Pistons end road trip with blowout win vs. Pelicans
item.description: NEW ORLEANS — Cade Cunningham stood in the visiting locker room at Frost Bank Center on Tuesday night, praising the Detroit Pistons ' depth. They had just pulled off one of their most impressive wins of the season, beating the San Antonio Spurs 107-93 . In the game, the Pistons relied on defense and character to overcome roster limitations from injuries. "I thought it was a great team win. We were down a lot of guys who bring a lot to this team every day. So, it was next man up," Cunningham said after the win. "We have the depth for that. I thought everyone who stepped onto the floor came with the right mindset, which added a lot to get this win." After a nationally televised victory, Cunningham's words proved to be more prophetic than he realized. Twenty-four hours later, Cunningham missed his first game of the season with right knee soreness. Even without their All-NBA guard, the Pistons showed more depth against the New Orleans Pelicans , which led to a 122-109 victory on Wednesday night, Nov. 18, inside Smoothie King Center. With the win, the Pistons improved to 10-4 overall and closed out their four-game road trip at 3-1. Coach J.B. Bickerstaff believes Cunningham knee injury isn’t serious enough to keep him sidelined for an extended period. His absence in the game against the Pelicans was mainly precautionary. Javonte Green started in place of the two-time All-Star and continued to prove why he is considered the team's Swiss Army Knife , able to fill any role needed. Green scored 18 points on 7-for-12 shooting, including three made 3-point field goals, along with seven rebounds and two steals. He scored 11 points in the second quarter. Six of those points came as the Pistons embarked on an 11-2 run, building a 57-48 lead by the 3:21 mark. Green started in the backcourt alongside Daniss Jenkins, who put together a near double-double performance with 17 points and nine assists. Although injuries have hampered the Pistons through the first 14 games, they got good news with the return of Isaiah Joe, who missed 10 straight games with a right hip contusion he sustained against the Philadelphia 76ers on Oct. 25. Joe returned at 7:14 of the first quarter to replace Kevin Huerter. On his first action, Joe stole the ball from Zion Williamson, then assisted on Jenkins' 3-point basket. Joe finished the game with 11 points on 3-for-6 shooting, 3-for-5 shooting from beyond the arc. One standout moment came at the 2:44 mark of the third quarter, when he made a 3-point field goal. This basket not only gave the Pistons an 85-77 lead but also halted the momentum the Pelicans were building during a 5-0 run midway through the period. In Cunningham's absence, six Pistons players scored in double figures. Paul Reed stepped up as the team's leading reserve, contributing 17 points, seven rebounds, and two blocks in just 20 minutes off the bench. Ausar Thompson followed his double-double performance against the Spurs with 10 points, six rebounds, and two steals. Du

item.title: AFC North Roundup: Bengals cruise to division lead; Browns stay in playoff hunt
item.description: Even with three teams still firmly in playoff contention, the AFC North race officially has a new favorite, while another team’s playoff hopes are all but officially over. With Cincinnati, Cleveland, and Pittsburgh all multiple games over .500 entering Week 11, there’s a very real chance we’ll see all three teams in the 2026-27 NFL Playoffs. As for the Ravens, their latest defeat effectively eliminated them from postseason contention. Here’s a look at what took place in Week 10 for the AFC North. Bengals steamroll Steelers Cincinnati brought the fireworks. Pittsburgh supplied the audience. With first place in the AFC North at stake Sunday night, the Bengals overwhelmed the Steelers, 38-18, improving to 7-2 with their fifth consecutive victory. Pittsburgh slipped to 6-3 after spending much of the evening trying to keep a divisional showdown from becoming an even bigger embarrassment. The final margin hardly captures how thoroughly Cincinnati controlled the game, which stood at 24-3 by halftime and 31-3 entering the fourth quarter. Joe Burrow gave Pittsburgh almost no room to breathe. He completed 35 of 44 passes for 409 yards and four touchdowns without an interception, piling up 302 yards and three scoring passes before halftime. Against a defense that had been one of the best in the NFL over the past four weeks, Cincinnati’s quarterback repeatedly delivered. The Bengals have now scored at least 30 points in five consecutive games, establishing a franchise record and giving their winning streak some serious offensive muscle. Ja’Marr Chase was the problem Pittsburgh never solved. His 11 receptions produced 231 yards, including a 53-yard gain that helped set up Cincinnati’s second touchdown. Chase Brown caught touchdown passes of two and four yards, while Drew Sample and Dohnte Meyers also scored through the air. That distribution made the Bengals especially difficult to contain: Chase could rip apart the coverage between the end zones, and Burrow had several other answers when Cincinnati reached scoring territory. The defense made sure Burrow’s production came with a comfortable cushion. Cincinnati limited Pittsburgh to 222 total yards and 17 first downs while generating three sacks. Jonathan Allen, Myles Murphy and Boye Mafe each brought down Aaron Rodgers, whose passing line finished at 16 completions in 32 attempts for 145 yards. Pittsburgh managed only a field goal through three quarters, leaving its offense with far too much ground to cover when the touchdowns finally arrived. Rodgers connected with DK Metcalf and Pat Freiermuth for fourth-quarter touchdowns, but Cincinnati answered the first of those scores with a one-yard Samaje Perine touchdown run. The Bengals finished with a 484-222 advantage in total offense and held the ball for 35:09. Those numbers tell the story of a team that dictated the evening on both sides of the ball. Cleveland spotted the Texans a 17-0 lead as C.J. Stroud threw early touchdown passes to Nico Collins and Xavier Hutchinson, but the Browns gradually erased the deficit. The victory kept the Browns within reach in the AFC North and served as a reminder that Cleveland remains part of the divisional conversation. Ravens suffer crippling loss vs. Chargers The Los Angeles Chargers snapped an 11-game losing streak Monday night, beating the Baltimore Ravens 23-20 for their first win of the season. Justin Herbert opened the scoring with a 22-yard touchdown run, and Omarion Hampton scored from the 1 on fourth down to give the Chargers a 17-7 lead late in the first half. Jacoby Brissett threw for 340 yards in his Ravens debut with Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley both on injured reserve. Baltimore went three-and-out on its first three possessions, but Henry scored twice, cutting the deficit to 23-20 with 10:23 remaining. Herbert finished with 129 passing yards and 51 rushing yards and went without an interception for the first time this season. The Ravens were approaching field-goal range with 2:03 left when Tarheeb Still stripped Zay Flowers after a catch near the Chargers’ 45-yard line. Elijah Molden recovered, and Herbert found former Raven Charlie Kolar for a first down to seal the win. Baltimore dropped to 4-6 with its fifth straight loss that likely ends their slim postseason dreams. AFC North Standings for Week 11

item.title: Sixers comeback thwarts Magic, Heat stay hot
item.description: LeBron James celebrates as the Philadelphia 76ers clinch a comeback win over the Orlando Magic (Rich Storry) The Philadelphia 76ers produced another double-digit comeback to defeat the Orlando Magic 121-116 and extend their lead at the top of the NBA Eastern Conference on Wednesday. Joel Embiid led the Sixers' scoring with 26 points while V.J. Edgecombe produced a decisive 13-point fourth-quarter burst in a 24-point performance as Philadelphia improved to 13-3. LeBron James also weighed in with 22 points after the Sixers recovered from a 17-point first-quarter deficit to claw their way back and extend their winning streak to four games. It was the sixth time this season the Sixers have come back to win after trailing by 10 points or more. Philadelphia coach Nick Nurse admitted he had feared the worst after watching a rampant Orlando score 40 points in the first quarter. "They were just flying around at 100 miles an hour and we weren't right," Nurse said. "They were really putting it on us. We had to try to change a few things and change the rhythm of the game. "Sometimes that works and sometimes it doesn't." Philadelphia trailed until midway through the fourth quarter, taking the lead with just over five minutes remaining via a Jabari Walker three-pointer. "We did a very nice job tonight of our execution offensively down the stretch," Nurse said. "We worked on some stuff this morning that we hadn't used before, and ran all that stuff very well and very calmly and with composure." The Miami Heat continued their march up the standings with a sixth straight win in a 137-130 defeat of the Milwaukee Bucks. Giannis Antetokounmpo finished with 27 points, 13 rebounds and nine assists against his former club while Bam Adebayo added 26 points. Davion Mitchell rattled in six three-pointers in a 24-point gem. Miami, who improved to 9-6, were always in control in a wire-to-wire victory that saw them lead by as many as 30 points in the fourth quarter. The Bucks have now lost 11 straight and remain at the foot of the table. In Cleveland, the Memphis Grizzlies improved to 11-4 with a 124-121 defeat of the Cavaliers in a game that saw the lead change hands 22 times. Cam Spencer led Memphis with 26 points as Donovan Mitchell's 34-point display for Cleveland ended in defeat. rcw/pst

item.title: ‘Best basketball in Dayton;’ Wright State rolls out new billboards amid team’s hot start
item.description: Drivers heading into Dayton on Interstate 75 or U.S. 35 may have spotted a new electronic billboard that may spark a debate among Dayton sports fans. [DOWNLOAD: Free WHIO-TV News app for alerts as news breaks ] News Center 7 first spotted a billboard promoting Wright State men’s basketball on the electronic billboard on I-75 southbound near Keowee Street. It features the retro Rowdy Raider logo, Wright State green and gold, and reads “The best basketball in Dayton.” TRENDING STORIES: New nonstop service from Cincinnati to Denver taking flight next year Man sentenced for ‘masterminding’ LEGO reselling theft scheme 3 men accused of pointing guns, then stealing from person, facing charges The website for Wright State Athletics was also listed, so News Center 7 reached out to the university about the billboard. A spokesperson confirmed that Wright State Athletics secured billboards along southbound I-75 and westbound U.S. 35 in an effort to “promote the men’s basketball program’s hot start across the Dayton region, and drive fans to show up and support Raider hoops.” The Raiders are currently 4-0 and have a chance to make program history tonight. A win against Malone at the Nutter Center tonight would secure the Raiders’ first 5-0 start since moving to Division I. “The billboard campaign is part of Wright State Athletics’ effort to grow the program’s visibility across the Dayton region. Dayton is a basketball town, and the billboards are a reminder that a team worth supporting is off to its best start in decades just up the road at the Nutter Center,” the spokesperson said in part. The spokesperson went on to speak on the city’s love of basketball, which once had a “crosstown stage” with the Raiders and the University of Dayton Flyers. “Wright State and Dayton met eight times from 1988 to 1997 in the Gem City Jam. The teams have not played since Dec. 13, 1997. Wright State Athletics would welcome the chance to bring the Gem City Jam back as a game that benefits Dayton Children’s Hospital and pediatric cancer research, putting the region’s passion for basketball behind a cause the whole community shares,” the spokespersons said. A spokesperson for UD athletics told News Center 7, “We have no comment on the business or operations of other programs.” [SIGN UP: WHIO-TV Daily Headlines Newsletter ]

item.title: Dodgers’ Mookie Betts Trade Looks Even More Lopsided After Latest Red Sox Move
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers’ trade for Mookie Betts has reached a new stage as all of the pieces sent to the Boston Red Sox have moved on. The Mookie Betts trade revisited The Dodgers sent former top prospect Alex Verdugo, Jeter Downs, Connor Wong, and cash for Mookie Betts, who was handed a 12-year, $365 million deal, along with an aging David Price and cash. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Dodgers Nation (@dodgersnation) LA won the trade after Betts’ first year, given how transformative he was and how he led the team to a World Series title in 2020. Until then, the Dodgers were a playoff team, but one that struggled once October hit; under Betts’ leadership, they have brought home three titles in his first seven years. Oct 31, 2025; Toronto, Ontario, CAN; Los Angeles Dodgers shortstop Mookie Betts (50) celebrates after defeating the Toronto Blue Jays in the 2025 MLB World Series at Rogers Center. Mandatory Credit: John E. Sokolowski-Imagn Images Price opted out of the 2020 season due to the COVID-19 pandemic, pitching only in 2021 (4.03 ERA) and 2022 (2.45 ERA). Betts, meanwhile, has three seasons with the Dodgers in which he finished in the top five in MVP voting. Where the Red Sox are now Things for the Red Sox’s players have not gone well. On Nov. 18, Connor Wong was designated for assignment, the last remaining player from the trade package who was still on the Red Sox. He played six years with Boston, posting a 4.2 bWAR during his time in Massachusetts. Alex Verdugo was a fine enough player for Boston, earning 8.1 bWAR in four seasons, but his bat declined sharply after a strong 2020 season. He was traded to the New York Yankees, a rare move for a player the Red Sox were willing to trade to their biggest rival, highlighting how bad Verdugo was at the plate. Jul 31, 2019; Denver, CO, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers center fielder Alex Verdugo (27) runs on a double in the sixth inning against the Colorado Rockies at Coors Field. Mandatory Credit: Isaiah J. Downing-USA TODAY Sports Finally, Jeter Downs played just 14 games for Boston in the big leagues before being designated for assignment in 2023. Downs has spent time in Japan over the last three years after leaving MLB, while Verdugo has bounced around the fringes of the league. With Wong now off the Sox’s roster, the trade for Betts looks all the more ridiculous in hindsight.

item.title: Lakers star Luka Doncic is having a month no other has had since 1960 Wilt Chamberlain
item.description: Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images Lakers star Luka Doncic is having a month no other has had since 1960 Wilt Chamberlain appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Luka Doncic is putting together a November for the history books with the Los Angeles Lakers , and the only name that can match it is Wilt Chamberlain . According to OptaSTATS , Doncic is averaging 40.4 points per game this month, and the Lakers have gone a perfect 8-0 in those games. The only other player in NBA history to average at least 40 points with an 8-0 team record through his first eight games of a month was Chamberlain in January 1960. Doncic’s latest outing came in Tuesday’s 118-114 overtime win over the Charlotte Hornets . He finished with 36 points, seven assists and six rebounds, and he set up Quentin Grimes for the game-tying 3-pointer at the end of regulation. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The month has been full of eye-popping performances. Doncic poured in 40 points, nine rebounds and seven assists in a win over the Sacramento Kings on Nov. 4 . Two days later, he exploded for a season-high 53 points against the Portland Trail Blazers, which also made him just the fourth player in Lakers history to score 40 or more in four straight games , joining Kobe Bryant, Elgin Baylor and George Mikan. Doncic has led the league in scoring for much of the season and is on pace to become the first player since Chamberlain to average 40 points over a full campaign. His previous career-best average was 33.9 points per game with the Dallas Mavericks in 2023-24. JJ Redick has marveled at his star . “It feels like a supernova, but it also feels normal. We live on a spaceship, and we’re going at the speed of light at all times when he’s on the court,” he said. Doncic, however, has kept his focus on the bigger picture. “As long as we win the game, I’m fine,” he said earlier this month. The Lakers have done plenty of that. Los Angeles has won nine straight games and owns the NBA’s best record at 13-3. Doncic and the Lakers will look to keep the streak going when they host the Utah Jazz on Wednesday. item.title: Lando Norris jokes he "found the limit of a champagne bottle" in Brazil podium mishap
item.description: Motorsport photo 2025 Formula 1 champion Lando Norris has joked about how he "found the limit of a champagne bottle" for the first time in his career during his chaotic podium celebrations at the Brazilian Grand Prix. The McLaren driver won from pole at Interlagos, but his trademark celebration went wrong. As he slammed the champagne bottle down on the floor, it shattered in his hands. To make matters worse, he then walked into the podium sparks. While speaking to the media during the drivers' press conference ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix, Norris was asked whether he would be changing his post-race celebrations after the incident. "Yeah, that was the hardest part of the weekend," he said. "I guess you'll find out on Sunday if I'm on the top step. I mean, I never do that if I'm not first. So I need to try to win another race for you guys to find out. "But for the first time in my career, I found the limit of a champagne bottle. So I'm happy I finally managed to find it." Lando Norris, McLaren Lando Norris, McLaren The Briton played down the effect of the sparks. "I did also walk into the sparks, which didn't help. But that was fine. I barely noticed it. I just kind of felt my ear was pretty hot, but it didn't burn me or anything," he said. "So yeah, not my finest couple of seconds, but also one for the memory books down the road. So I saved a little bit of the bottle. There's probably still some up on the podium in Brazil, but yeah, you'll find out when I next win." The incident came at the end of what Norris called "a mega weekend". He took pole position in the wet and went on to win the race, his third victory of the season. Norris admitted, however, that McLaren had not quite matched Mercedes for outright dry pace in Brazil, and that the tricky conditions had helped. With three races remaining in the 2026 season, Norris currently sits sixth in the drivers' standings. To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Granby/Canton vs. CREC football game moved to Veterans Stadium in New Britain
item.description: Granby/Canton's football game against CREC on Friday, Nov. 20, 2026, has been moved from Trinity College in Hartford to Veterans Stadium in New Britain. (Getty Images) Granby/Canton's football game against CREC on Friday night has been moved to Veterans Stadium in New Britain. The game will kick off at 6 p.m., Friday. The game was originally scheduled to be played at Trinity College in Hartford on Friday, with CREC as the host team, but CREC honored a request to move the game, according to CIAC executive director Glenn Lungarini. "The CIAC worked with CREC and Granby Memorial administration to move their game to Veterans Stadium in New Britain," Lungarini said. "CREC athletic administration was responsive and understanding of the request to move the game. The CIAC is providing CREC with financial and personnel support for that game." Granby/Canton is 7-2 and in fourth place in the Class S standings. The Bears can clinch a playoff berth with a win over CREC (0-8). Granby/Canton had its last game against the Hartford co-op at Weaver suspended after a fight broke out in the fourth quarter. The game was deemed completed the next day with Granby/Canton awarded the win 19-12, the score at the time of the suspension. Another fight occurred following the game and led to the arrests of two juveniles, one of whom had a loaded semi-automatic gun in a backpack . Police did not release the names of those arrested because they are juveniles. The Hartford co-op was scheduled to play Coginchaug/East Hampton/Classical at Coginchaug High School as part of the Week 11 schedule, but that game has been cancelled with the Coginchaug co-op awarded a forfeit win . item.title: ‘Get negative’ – Bam Adebayo and Tyler Herro ignoring each other after their fight has fans hyped
item.description: Photo by Melissa Tamez/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Bam Adebayo and Tyler Herro had a falling out following the latter’s trade to the Milwaukee Bucks, which allegedly ended in a violent altercation. Adebayo and Herro allegedly got into it in Las Vegas during the NBA Summer League, with reports suggesting their relationship had deteriorated to such an extent after seven years as teammates. However, how the two acted around each other in their first game against each other has many fans hoping this could be the start of another NBA rivalry. Bam Adebayo and Tyler Herro ignoring each other doesn’t shock NBA fans Ahead of the Miami Heat’s game against the Milwaukee Bucks, fans had their eyes glued to Bam Adebayo and Tyler Herro, as this was set to be their first time engaging with each other in public since the incident in Las Vegas. Unsurprisingly, the two haven’t made amends just yet, as both stars ignored each other in the pre-game warm-up and proceeded to greet all the other players. Understandably, this moment had many NBA fans talking, as they felt that Bam and Herro were not going to be on the same page. One fan seemed to enjoy the hostility, simply remarking: “Let’s get negative.” Another fan likened their silence to a situation most people in life will have experienced: “Bam and Herro treated pregame like a group chat nobody’s replying to.” A third fan seemed to criticise both players for still harbouring a grudge: “NBA players are the softest people on earth.” A fourth fan suggested this interaction was a preview of how Adebayo was going to approach the game: “So Bam knew he was going to be on b******* from jump.” Hilariously, a fifth fan compared their feud to another high-profile NBA falling out: “Walmart Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown.” And lastly, one Miami Heat fan lamented the state of their relationship: “Bam and Herro acting like strangers at the tip when they are supposed to run the pick-and-roll together.” At the time of this writing, Adebayo is out of the game as the Heat are on track to defeat the Bucks by a significant 20-point margin. Herro did not have a good game against his former team, scoring just eight points on 4/11 shooting, while going 0/5 from deep. On the other end, Adebayo led the Heat in scoring, putting up 26 points on 7/15 shooting from the field and 3/8 shooting from beyond the arc. If their rivalry proves to be a years-long chess game with both sides going back and forth, Adebayo has just made the first big move over Herro. item.title: Northwestern football’s Aidan Chiles to miss 3rd-straight week with upper body injury
item.description: Oregon defensive back Peyton Woodyard, left, stops Northwest quarterback Aidan Chiles as the Oregon Ducks host the Northwestern Wildcats on Oct. 31, 2026, at Autzen Stadium in Eugene, Oregon. Northwestern football’s Aidan Chiles to miss 3rd-straight week with upper body injury appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Coach David Braun ’s Northwestern Wildcats scored a big early season over Colorado in celebration of his contract extension, but things have taken a downturn in recent weeks. The Wildcats won four in a row near midseason leading to an epic Braun speech after beating Penn State, but reality has set in among a key injury to QB Aidan Chiles. Chiles got word that his upper body injury still isn’t healed well enough to play ahead of Week 5’s tilt against the Minnesota Golden Gophers at Huntington Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, as shared by Pete Thamel of ESPN. He was listed as “out” for the game along with fellow Wildcats players RB Daniel Anderson, LB Max Mohring, LB Qayvier Johnson, OL Ozomo Oratokhai, and TE Chris Petrucci. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) DB Ore Adeyi and DB Josh Fussell were listed as questionable, along with LB Matthew Smith, for the Wildcats’ road game against PJ Fleck’s Gophers. Fortunes shift quickly in the world of Division-I college football, something Braun and Chiles have found out the hard way. Chiles was nearing Heisman Trophy status and helped lead Northwestern into the college football power rankings earlier in the season, now his playing status is in doubt, as is Northwestern’s future as a Big Ten contender. Nicco Marchiol has shown flashes of strong play in relief of Chiles, but if there’s one thing Northwestern fans have learned from his injury, it’s the value the former MSU and Oregon State QB provides to his team, something the Wildcats will need to sort out and try to replace as the season comes to a close. item.title: Home ice not nice for Wings; fall 4-1 to Boston
item.description: DETROIT - Returning home after a long road trip didn't prove to be any sort of tonic for the Red Wings. The Wings took an early lead Wednesday, Nov. 18, but couldn't hold it, as Boston rolled to a 4-1 victory. J.J. Peterka and Pavel Zacha (power play) scored Boston goals in the second period, erasing a 1-0 Wings lead. David Pastrnak then provided some cushion in the period giving the Bruins a 3-1 lead. Casey Mittelstadt ended the scoring with his eighth goal, into an empty net, with 54.8 seconds remaining. The Wings (8-11-3, 19 points) lost their sixth game in the last seven, and seven of their last nine. Goaltender Daniil Tarasov stopped 26 shots for the Wings, keeping the game tight in the first period with several big saves. Boston's Jeremy Swayman made 19 saves. The Bruins (14-7-1, 29 points) ended a three-game losing streak. Lucas Raymond scored his ninth goal in the first period, giving the Wings an early lead. Keegan Kolesar got the puck ahead to Andrew Copp, who with a Bruins' defenseman pinching, went on a 2-on-1 rush with Raymond. Copp fed Raymond for a one-timer that sailed past Swayman at 16:58. But the Bruins rallied in the middle period. Peterka tied it with his sixth goal. Mason Lohrei found Peterka skating down wing, and Peterka blistered a shot that snuck just under the crossbar and over Tarasov, at 2:49. After the Bruins killed a Wings' power play, a Moritz Seider tripping penalty put the Bruins on the power play. Zacha scored his sixth goal, at 11:48, after Pastrnak threw the puck at net and it bounced off a pad straight to Zacha in the slot. Pastrnak made it 3-1 in the third period with his 10th goal. Lohrei skated into the zone and found Pastrnak, who skated into the slot and blasted a shot past Tarasov at 5:11. tkulfan@detroitnews.com @tkulfan This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Home ice not nice for Wings; fall 4-1 to Boston

item.title: Red Wings Centennial Game Not One for the Ages
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect DETROIT — The Detroit Red Wings’ Centennial celebration included honoring the franchise’s great players, such as Gordie Howe , Steve Yzerman , Nick Lidstrom and Terry Sawchuk among others. Scotty Bowman, now 93, joined the party with a video message that included an introduction of Grind Line members Darren McCarty, Joe Kocur, Kris Draper and Kirk Maltby. Even long-time anthem singer Karen Newman was in the house to sign the Star Spangled Banner. All that was missing was a Red Wings’ performance for the ages. Daniil played well for two periods, but it wasn’t enough to prevent a sixth Red Wings loss in seven games. The Boston Bruins, Detroit’s opponent in their first NHL game, used second-period goals by J.J. Peterka and Pavel Zacha (power play) to down the Red Wings 4-1. The Red Wings had claimed a 1-0 first period lead when Lucas Raymond cashed in on a two-on-one break for his sixth point in the past six games. Andrew Copp had set-up Raymond with a perfect cross-ice feed. Takeaways Tarasov’s numbers are significantly better than John Gibson ‘s numbers this season. But he probably needed to win this game to earn a third consecutive start. . . The Bruins ended a three-game losing streak with the win. . . . Tarasov made five saves against David Pastrnak before he scored in the third period Key Stat The Bruins were one-for-one on the power play and the Red Wings didn’t convert on their only power play. Key Moment Zacha’s go-ahead power play goal, scored from the blue paint, is particularly frustrating when you consider the Bruins have one of the league’s weakest power plays. They were at just over 17% coming into the game. Up Next The Red Wings face the New York Islanders at home Saturday. item.title: UConn Huskies: Why One February Contest Will Be Particularly Emotional
item.description: On Feb. 12, 2027, the UConn Huskies men's hockey program will be part of an emotional Hockey East contest against Boston College. Before that game, the Eagles will retire the No. 13 uniform of Johnny Gaudreau. Gaudreau, 31, and his brother Matthew, 29, were both killed in August of 2024 when they were hit by a car in New Jersey. They had been riding bikes. Matthew also played hockey at Boston College. About Johnny Gaudreau at Boston College Nicknamed "Johnny Hockey," Gaudreau was one of the best college players we've seen in the last quarter century. He spent three years with the Eagles from 2011-14, winning the national championship as a freshman in 2012. He won the 2014 Hobey Baker Award, which is the hockey equivalent of the Heisman Trophy. He scored 175 points while in Chestnut Hill, including a ridiculous 80-point season in 2013-14. He had 36 goals and 44 assists that season. He helped BC with the famous "Beanpot Trophy" three times. Boston College Eagles forward Johnny Gaudreau (13) shoots as Minnesota Gophers goalie Kent Patterson (35) defends in the second period during the semifinals of the 2012 Frozen Four at Tampa Bay Times Forum. Kim Klement-USA TODAY Sports About Johnny Gaudreau in the NHL A fourth-round pick in 2011, Gaudreau played 11 years in the NHL with the Calgary Flames and Columbus Blue Jackets. He was a seven-time All-Star who led the league in +/- in 2021-22. He got to the playoffs five different times in his career, and he tallied 243 goals and an even 500 assists. Gaudreau getting another honor as well Johnny and Matthew will get honored with a life-sized statue outside their childhood rink in Sewell, N.J. It will be unveiled early in 2028. About the UConn men's hockey program The Huskies are off to a tough start in 2026-27, as they sit at 4-7-1 overall and 2-5-1 inside Hockey East play. They will be back in action on Thursday night at home against the University of New Hampshire. Faceoff is set for 7 p.m. ET. They'll play New Hampshire again on Saturday, but that game will be in Durham, N.H. UConn will then go to Ireland over the Thanksgiving holiday, as they will participate in the "Friendship Four" with Colgate, Providence and Minnesota-Duluth. Elsewhere in UConn Athletics... The UConn women's basketball team, now ranked No. 7 nationally, will open up Big East play on Friday night at home against Seton Hall (8 p.m. ET). The Huskies are coming off an 18-point loss against Louisville last Sunday night, dropping them to 3-2 overall. Not only have the Huskies dropped two games already, they've also missed out on two recruits this week.

Sir Matt Busby stepped aside as manager of the 1968 European Cup-winning side, but stayed on as a director, just as Sir Alex Ferguson did, watching from the Old Trafford directors’ box as successors tried and failed. item.title: ‘The game is in danger’: PFA head Maheta Molango on Fifa, Infantino and football’s future
item.description: At a potentially critical juncture for football, the PFA’s chief executive talks about the organisation, wider fears in the game and why the Folarin Balogun affair was ‘scandalous’ After five years in charge of the Professional Footballers’ Association, what has Maheta Molango learned? “The game is in danger,” the 44-year-old says. “I’ve learned that the game I loved and led me to first play and then advise and then lead a club and today to lead the PFA, is in danger because it is being forgotten.” In 2026, with football ubiquitous on all platforms, with a World Cup that generated $15bn (£11.4bn) in revenue, and with attendances across the English pyramid growing year on year, it may seem hard to imagine forgetting about the game. But Molango’s unique perspective as head of the players’ union for England and Wales observes a different picture; one where the future of the sport is being determined not by what will maintain its popularity, but what will make the most money. item.title: Pocognoli’s aspiration for how Scotland must play is in danger of becoming unworkable
item.description: The 4-0 debacle against Switzerland has added to the tactical concerns about the head coach’s suitability, just six games into the job The Scottish Football Association can only cling to a lesson from the past when assessing a worrying international window. Steve Clarke was beleaguered during his early games in charge. Successive 4-0 defeats by Belgium and Russia in 2019 left Clarke with the sense he should have stayed in club management. A revival meant Clarke led his country to three out of four tournaments. There are, however, fundamental differences between the story of Clarke and that being delivered by Sébastien Pocognoli. Clarke was a pragmatist, whose decades in coaching suggested he had the wherewithal to revive Scotland. Pocognoli, six games into his tenure, is in danger of lurching into the territory of dreamy ideologue whose aspiration for how Scotland must play is unworkable. The meek nature of Scotland’s collapse in the 4-0 loss to a second-string Switzerland was lamentable. The Belgian’s assessment, with overpraise a key theme, raised eyebrows. Continue reading...

item.title: Reliving the drama: England and Argentina stars watch 1986 classic with fresh eyes
item.description: A new film about the historic World Cup quarter-final clash finds new angles for a new generation “Is there anything new to say about it?” Gary Lineker asked the producer Flora Fernandez-Marengo when she first approached him to take part in The Match, a documentary about the 1986 World Cup quarter-final between England and Argentina. Flora told an audience at the London film festival premiere of the film that she played her best card then and showed Lineker an image of Maradona with Queen in 1981, during the band’s tour of Argentina. Maradona wearing a union jack T-shirt and Freddie Mercury an Argentina strip. It worked. Lineker said yes. The rock’n’roll angle, with Brian May as a talking head, is one of the very few details the film-makers added to Andrés Burgo’s book, The Match, on which the documentary is based. The directors Juan Cabral and Santiago Franco play with the timeline, hopping between past and present across 91 minutes, the exact duration of the match itself. Anecdotes that now form part of Argentina’s football folklore are spliced with excellent archive material. Continue reading...

item.title: Janine van Wyk: ‘Our rooms were empty … no mattresses, no lightbulbs and not a drop of water’
item.description: In an extract from the former South Africa captain’s book, she details less than ideal Wafcon 2006 preparations I was just a year into my international career when we qualified for my first Wafcon, which was then called the African Women’s Championship (AWC) and was held in Nigeria in 2006. I was extremely excited but very nervous to participate in this tournament, more so when it was announced that we would be in the same group as the hosts, and would play them last in the group. As it turned out, it would be the game that decided who finished top of the group. By then we had beaten Algeria 4-0 and Equatorial Guinea 2-0 and had to travel to Delta State to take on the hosts. I’d heard that Nigeria was the toughest country to travel to and I was about to realise why. It’s become common knowledge that South Africans and Nigerians are massive rivals on the football field but also don’t really get on off it. Continue reading...

item.title: Max Dowman shines in England colours and sends another record tumbling
item.description: Midfielder’s under-21s winner eclipsed Jude Bellingham’s mark and there was other talent to admire against France There may have been an Mbappé on the pitch – Ethan, the younger brother of Kylian, with whom he shares a near-identical gait – but by the end there was only one precocious talent on the lips of those watching England overcome France in their under-21s clash. Max Dowman had done it again, lighting up another game, this time in filthy conditions at Ashton Gate. It was fitting he had the final say in a 3-2 win. The noise that accompanied his match-winning goal? Well, beyond the palpable excitement in the stands in Bristol, that would be the sound of the teenager sending yet another record tumbling. Which one takes your fancy? Take your pick. At 14, playing for Arsenal Under-19s, he became the Uefa Youth League’s youngest goalscorer. This time last year, after taking to the field at Slavia Prague aged 15 and 308 days , Dowman became the youngest player to feature in the Champions League. In March, six months on from his professional debut, he became the Premier League’s youngest goalscorer . He is the youngest player to earn a Premier League winner’s medal. Last month he was presented with three Guinness World Records. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘He wants to change lives’: the story behind Bukayo Saka’s Sócrates award
item.description: By supporting the non-profit BigShoe, the Arsenal forward has earned deserved plaudits for his social conscience Valerie Fiesser will never forget her surprise when Bukayo Saka contacted her out of the blue in 2022, asking whether he could help support a project in Nigeria. “I remember thinking: ‘Is this really Bukayo writing us an email?’” says the president of BigShoe, a non-profit organisation based in Frankfurt that has helped more than 10,000 children worldwide. “But that’s how he is. He’s always asking what more we can do.” Four years on from that unexpected email, Fiesser was given the secret task of reaching out for a letter for Saka to read from the podium when he was presented with the Sócrates award at last month’s Ballon d’Or ceremony in London for his humanitarian work. She got the words from Byiringiro, a 14-year-old from Rwanda who had his eyesight restored after having surgery thanks to a BigShoe initiative. Continue reading...

item.title: Thomas Frank’s to-do list: lift mood, fix defence and fire up Sarr and Mateta
item.description: Seeking redemption after failing at Spurs, newly installed Crystal Palace manager has a tough challenge ahead Thomas Frank promised his wife, Nanna, he would take a year’s sabbatical after being sacked by Tottenham in February , but he couldn’t wait that long. Having received a reported £8m payoff from Spurs, he kept an extremely low profile in the first few months after an experience at the club that sources close to the 53‑year‑old have described as “traumatic”. Frank broke his silence at the start of June with a statement released by the League Managers Association. It said he would cover the World Cup for the BBC (thereby going head-to-head with Ange Postecoglou, his predecessor at Spurs, who worked for ITV) before “experiencing the Tour de France”, a lifelong passion. Frank usually preferred to run to Brentford’s training ground and home matches from his home in East Sheen during a nine‑year spell as assistant and then manager, but he occasionally cycled because it helped to clear his head. item.title: Spain in pain as historic run ends but De la Fuente feels best is yet to come
item.description: While the head coach, players and Spanish press were magnanimous in defeat, there was pride mixed in with disappointment – and confidence the future is still bright “With every game, defeat gets closer,” Luis de la Fuente had said and on Sunday night it finally came. Spain had lost only one competitive game since Scotland in March 2023 back when the coach hadn’t won anything and didn’t look like he ever would – and that solitary loss was on penalties in the 2025 Nations League final . Statistically, they said, penalties don’t count, so while Portugal lifted the trophy that night, the team that won the European Championship and World Cup in the summers either side also claimed a Fifa record of 44 official games unbeaten. And then England turned up at the Metropolitano . A night that started with Iker Casillas, Fernando Torres and Fernando Llorente handing the World Cup to Unai Simón ended with Spain trying to overhaul a shock 3-0 deficit. Against 10 men and led by a superb Lamine Yamal, Spain made De la Fuente think for a while that they would too, but it wasn’t to be. Continue reading...

item.title: Do good club managers necessarily make good international managers? | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: In a mailbag edition of our newsletter, we look at Mauricio Pochettino, Pep Guardiola’s international credentials and the lack of elite English managers Sign up for our free newsletter here Who should replace Mauricio Pochettino as the USMNT manager? – Tom S Although the salary I’m sure will be excellent, I think the US job is going to be a really difficult sell to a top-level coach. The 2030 World Cup is a long way away and I’m not sure the Concacaf Nations League, the Gold Cup or even the 2028 Copa América carry much appeal for a manager with European experience or aspirations. But I’m not entirely sure that sort of coach is necessarily a great idea. The last two World Cups, after all, have been won by low-key coaches who have come from within the federation and have worked with many of the players at youth level. That’s the positive from appointing from within; appointing from without is almost certainly more expensive and there’s the danger the next foreign manager does just what Mauricio Pochettino does, and has his head turned by the first vaguely attractive European job that comes calling. item.title: Familiarity of Doha drives home just how far Socceroos have come in recent years | Joey Lynch
item.description: There is increasing evidence of an evolution not only in approach but also mentality, highlighted by a return to the scene of Asian Cup heartbreak Last week’s 3-0 dismissal of Qatar at the Abdullah bin Khalifa Stadium marked the first time the Socceroos had returned to the Gulf state since their heartbreaking elimination from the Asian Cup just under three years ago. Back then, coach Graham Arnold called Doha a “home away from home” after they relocated there during the Covid pandemic, and went so far as to suggest that they would have some form of advantage at the 2022 World Cup as a result. Wandering around the city in 2026, memories rush back of Socceroos fans becoming eager participants in the takeover of the city’s souks during the World Cup. So too the feelings of sadness to see the birds still cooped up in small cages at the nearby bird market. It evokes recollections of trips on the red Metro line out to the Al Janoub Stadium in Al Wakrah, aided by the faded posters and stickers celebrating the 2022 tournament’s arrival that to this day can still be seen in shopfronts. There’s the excitement, for some, when a stray cat reminds you just how personable the local felines can be, as well as the sense of unease that remains whenever one pauses to reflect on how all this was built and the hands that did so. item.title: WSL talking points: Chelsea’s gamble pays off and have Arsenal lost fear factor?
item.description: Blues beat champions after bold substitution and Gunners’ home struggles continue with fifth consecutive WSL draw Sonia Bompastor attempted to deflect suggestions that the removal of Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes into Chelsea’s top-of-the-table clash with Manchester City was tactical, but few were convinced by the claim that it was down to injury. The manager said the centre-back, who had not asked to come off and walked straight down the tunnel, had taken a knock to the head in training and been assessed and cleared, but that during the game “she was not herself”. On came Veerle Buurman and the threat of Khadija Shaw was nullified, the Dutch defender restricting the golden boot favourite so well that Shaw did not manage a shot on target. Bompastor said after the game that she had not spoken to Buchanan but that she would “explain myself to her”. “I always have good relationships with the players, bring them clarity, and I’m always direct and honest so they have the information,” she said. “It won’t be any different.” Enforced or not, the substitution was a huge gamble that paid off, even after the loss of Melvine Malard to injury in the first half reduced their number of remaining in-game substitution windows to one. Set up in a compact, attack-minded formation they carried credible threat against hosts managed by Ralf Rangnick, but to nobody’s great surprise Sasa Kalajdzic broke the deadlock, scrambling home the winner from a needlessly conceded and poorly defended corner. item.description: Plus: more speedy marathons by footballers, headed goals of the season and chairs acting as managers Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Which club team has had the most international captains playing together at one time?” asks MH Zahid. “Conversely, which international team has had the most club captains in its starting lineup at one time?” A quick web search finds a fuss being made in various corners of the internet of Chelsea’s 2009-10 squad because it contained six national team captains in Michael Ballack (Germany), Petr Cech (Czech Republic), Didier Drogba (Côte d’Ivoire), Branislav Ivanovic (Serbia), Mikel John Obi (Nigeria) and John Terry (England). These are, indeed, six people who captained their countries, playing together at one time, but crucially they were not all international captains at that time, which because we like to have our hands bound as tight as possible – no questions please – mean they are disqualified from this particular tournament. Ivanovic, you see, was not named Serbia captain until 2012 and Mikel, who was but a whippersnapper at 22 when the 2009-10 season started, was still seven years from getting his hands on the Nigeria armband. item.title: Football comes together across Spain to honour Jesús de Miguel: ‘We’ve seen how fragile life is’
item.description: Across La Liga and beyond this weekend, footballers took to the field knowing it could have been them In the final few minutes before stepping into the arena once more, heading out for his 199th Osasuna match on Saturday evening, the man who has scored more first division goals than anyone in their history stopped his teammates for a moment and told them what it meant to wear the shirt. “This is very important,” Ante Budimir began as the dressing room, their sanctuary, fell silent around him. “We don’t have this shirt today for the sake of it. He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be. Boys, we were not chosen: not us, not him. Let us go, gratefully. Without thought. We have a grand day before us.” With that, Osasuna’s players turned left out of the room, where they were joined in the tunnel by footballers from Athletic Club, rivals from the north, and together they went out past the little shrine of Saint Fermin on to the field. They carried white lilies and all wore the same white shirts with a No 9 on the back, a black ribbon and the name of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who died after a collision on the pitch five days earlier at the age of 30. At almost exactly the same time, 2,000km away to the west, Tenerife’s squad were walking out at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López in Santa Cruz. They did not have anyone alongside them, wore black suits not white shirts and did not have a game to play either, not this week. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Delap’s talents resurface in style, Gómez delights Brighton with more fireworks, and hair-pulling confusion at Everton It would have been very easy for Oliver Glasner to lose patience with Liam Delap. The forward is still only 23, yet the days when he was rattling in 12 in a Premier League season for Ipswich have come to seem a very long time ago (and his six games for Manchester City even longer). A season at Chelsea had left him bereft of confidence, an odd mix of diffidence and overaggression, devoid of composure in the box, arms flailing like a broken windmill. But the old gifts have not left him. Both goals on Saturday were the result of great muscular surges and if the first finish seemed essentially about hitting the ball as hard as possible on target, the second was a precise – and still powerful – finish in off the far post. After games such as this it’s possible to imagine him as England’s long-term replacement for Harry Kane. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
